plain.text: Abraham was very old, and the LORD had blessed him in every way. He asked his chief servant to swear that he would not find a wife for Isaac among the Canaanites, but would go to Abraham's relatives and find a wife there. The God of heaven would send his angel ahead of him. The servant took ten camels loaded with gifts and travelled to the town of Nahor. He made the camels kneel by the well in the evening, when the women came out to draw water. He prayed, "LORD, God of my master Abraham, give me success today and show kindness to my master. May the young woman I ask for a drink, who says, 'Drink, and I'll water your camels too,' be the one you have chosen for Isaac."

Before he had finished praying, Rebekah came out with her jar. She was the granddaughter of Abraham's brother Nahor, and very beautiful. The servant asked for a drink, and she said, "Drink, my lord," and then offered to water all his camels. The servant watched in silence. When he learned who she was, he bowed and worshipped the LORD, who had led him straight to his master's relatives. Rebekah ran home. Her brother Laban came and welcomed the servant. The servant would not eat until he had told his story: Abraham's blessing, the oath, his prayer at the well, and how Rebekah had answered exactly as he had prayed. Laban and Bethuel said, "This is from the LORD." The servant gave gifts. When the family wanted Rebekah to stay ten more days, they asked her, "Will you go with this man?" "I will go," she said. They blessed her and she set out with her nurse and servants.

Isaac was out in the field one evening to meditate. He looked up and saw camels coming. Rebekah saw Isaac, got down from her camel and covered herself with her veil. The servant told Isaac everything. Isaac brought her into his mother Sarah's tent, and she became his wife. He loved her, and Isaac was comforted after his mother's death.

summary.bigIdea: God answers the servant's prayer and guides him to Rebekah, who becomes Isaac's wife.
points: Abraham's servant prays for guidance at the well.
Rebekah shows generous kindness, answering his prayer exactly.
Rebekah chooses to go, Isaac loves her, and he is comforted after Sarah's death.
summary.reflection: The servant prayed specifically and then praised God when he saw the answer. When did you last thank God for answered prayer?
